ORD This petition under Article 226 of Constitution of India has been filed seeking following relief(s):-
1.

To seek writ in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to implement the order of Establishment officer dated 2.6.1977 whereby it has been clearly directed that land of petitioner is their Patta Bhoomi, hence the same may be bifurcated from the boundary of the Forest Reserve.

2. To issue writ in nature of mandamus directing the respondent that if the land of petitioner is required for the purpose of Forest Reserve, acquisition proceeding may be done in accordance with law as per the new policy and guidelines in the matter and that the petitioner must be paid proper compensation for his land.
3. The respondents be directed to not interfere with agricultural activities on the said land by the petitioner as the land is the only means of livelihood for the petitioner.
4. To grant any other relief deemed fit and proper in the circumstances of the present case.
2. It is the case of petitioner that he belongs to Schedule Tribe staying in the outskirts of the forest and carry out agricultural activities.
Since year 1950, khasra No.140 was registered in the name of his father namely Jairam Bhurtiya.
Petitioner claims himself to be the sole legal heir of his father who has already passed away.
Since various nearby lands are the forest lands, therefore Government has notified the reserve forest as per Section 4 of Indian Forest Act.

sentences.text: No proper proceedings were initiated for acquisition of the land of petitioner.

In the year 1970-71, when father of petitioner came to know about the fact that his land which was granted to him on patta has been notified as reserve forest, then he filed an application before the Forest Establishment Officer for release of his land from reserve forest.
One H.P. Agnihotri, Deputy Collector was declared as Establishment Officer.
Application filed by father of petitioner was registered as case No.94/70-71 block Deva Van Mandal Sidhi.

Vide order dated 02/06/1977,
Establishment Officer declared various khasra numbers of village Kharbar as patta bhumi.

Land of petitioner i.e. khasra No.140/2 area 3.5 acres was also found to be patta bhumi and accordingly,
Forest Establishment Officer declared khasra No.140/2 area 3.5 acres as patta bhumi which is evident from order dated 02/06/1977 passed in case No.94/70-71.
Authorities did not follow the direction of the Establishment Officer.
However, petitioner continued to be in cultivating possession of the land.
In the year 2015, petitioner was stopped from cultivating crops on the said land by the local forest officer by saying that the said land is under reserve forest.

In the year 2015, present petitioner made an application before Regional Director and Deputy Director of Sanjay Tiger Reserve Sidhi by contending that the land of petitioner has not been bifurcated/ removed from reserve forest as per order dated 02/06/1977 and also prayed for grant of permission for cultivation of crops.

On the basis of said application made by the present petitioner, Deputy Director, Sanjay Tiger Reserve wrote a letter to Assistant Director and Sub Divisional Forest Officer Majhouli thereby directing the Authorities to send a spot inspection report on the following issues:-
(i) GPS reading of khasra No.140/2 area 3.5 acres from all the four corners.
(ii) Distance of the aforesaid land inside the reserve forest.
(iii) Reasons for stopping the petitioner from cultivating the land and if the land is inside the forest area, then its compartment number.
3. Since no action took place, again petitioner moved an application on 20/08/2018 before the Collector in Jansunwai.
Then again on 17/09/2018 petitioner made an application by giving reference of his application dated 18/12/2015 to the Regional Director as well as Deputy Director Sidhi pleading the same grievances.
However, no report has been submitted so far.
Again petitioner made an application on 15/10/2018 for removing the land from the area of reserve forest.
By order dated 05/03/2019, information was given by Forest Range Officer to Joint Director, Sanjay Tiger Reserve Sidhi informing him about the GPS reading of the land.

It was further mentioned that the said land is within the forest area number P.F. 509 and since the land in dispute is situated inside the forest area, therefore petitioner has been stopped from cultivating the land and accordingly, it was prayed that since the land in dispute is situated inside the forest area, therefore direction was sought for correction of map as well as for transfer of old munnaras.
However, it is submitted by counsel for the petitioner that no action has been taken.

4. Accordingly, it is prayed that since the Establishment Officer by order dated 02/06/1977 had specifically pointed out that it is a patta bhumi, therefore if the land of the petitioner is required for the purposes of reserve forest, then acquisition proceedings may be done.

sentences.text: Respondents have filed their return and claimed that khasra No.140/2 is a forest land.
In some records, khasra No.140/2 was recorded as land of petitioner granted on patta.
It is the case of petitioner that by order dated 02/05/1958 passed by Naib Tehsildar Majouli, land admeasuring 3.5 acres was granted to his late father Jairam Bhurtiya.
In order to verify as to whether petitioner is entitled to retain 3.5 acres of land by virtue of patta alleged to be given to his father or not, a Committee was constituted on 10/09/2020.

The said Committee was consisting of SDO (Revenue)
Kusmi, Assistant Director, SDO Forest Majhouli, Tehsildar Kusmi and Forest Range Officer Dubri.

The Committee examined the entire records pertaining to the land in dispute since the time of his Highness Rewa Darbar and thereafter came to conclusion that initially the entire khasra No.140 was reserve forest land which was declared by the Rewa Darbar way back in the year 1935.
Khasra of mouja Kharbar of khasra No.140 has also been filed to show that khasra No.140 was notified as land of forest.

Khasras of the year 1956-57, 1958-59 up to 1960-61 have also been placed on record in which khasra No.140 was shown as forest land but in column 5, name of Jairam was recorded over the piece of 3.50 acres of land.

Since the land which was already notified as forest land cannot be converted and allotted on patta to any person without de-notifying the said land from forest area,
therefore it appears that under some misconception the order granting patta might have been passed, but there is no specific order to show that under what provision of law, name of Jairam was recorded as bhumiswami in respect of 3.50 acres of land forming part of khasra No.140/2.
After considering the entire record, the Committee gave a categorical finding that since very inception land was recorded as forest land.

For the purposes of tracing out 3.5 acres of land alleged to be khasra No.140/2, GPS reading was taken and ultimately, it was found that out of four points, three points were found as forest land in forest compartments bearing 219 and one part was found in forest compartment 509.
The area of 3.5 acres alleged to be granted in favour of petitioner was found within 270 meters boundary of forest area.
Copy of report dated 23/12/2021 has also been filed as Annexure-R/6.
Thus, it is clear that entire khasra No.140 including khasra No.140/2 is a forest land and patta cannot be given in that regard.

6. Considered the submissions made by counsel for the parties.
7.
The only controversy involved in the present case is as to whether khasra No.140/2 is a forest land or is a patta land.
8. Petitioner has not filed any order of the competent Authority by which patta was granted to his late father.
The entire claim of petitioner is based on the khasra entries.
9. It is well established principle of law that khasra entry is not a document of title and it is made only for fiscal purposes.
10. Furthermore, in none of the khasra entry, the basis of recording of name of father of petitioner has been mentioned.
Thus, it appears that the name of father of petitioner was mentioned in the khasra entries without there being any order by the competent Authority.
11. Respondents have filed a copy of Rewa Raj Gazette Part-I dated 25th May, 1935, according to which khasra No.140 was declared as forest land under Section 20 of Rewa State Forest Act, 1935.

of year 1956-57, land has been recorded as forest land but in column 5, name of father of petitioner was mentioned.
However, there is nothing in this khasra panchshala to show that on the basis of which order, name of father of petitioner was recorded.
Once the land was already declared as forest land, then unless and until it is de-notified, the same cannot be converted into a revenue land.
12. Counsel for petitioner could not point out as to how order of the Establishment Officer would amount to de-notifying the khasra No.140/2 as forest land.

Although petitioner by filing rejoinder has also challenged the constitution of Committee by saying that there was no independent member in the said Committee nor any villager or local person was included but in the considered opinion of this Court, there is no defect in constitution of the Committee.
The Committee was merely required to submit the spot inspection report with regard to location of the land.

Petitioner has not challenged the findings given by the Committee.
13.
As already pointed out, except khasra panchashala, there is nothing on record to show that father of petitioner was validly given patta of khasra No.140/2.
Even otherwise, there is no document on record to show that any patta was ever given to father of petitioner.
Furthermore, khasra No.140/2 has also been notified as reserve forest area and said notification has not been challenged by petitioner.
Unless and until the notification is challenged, no relief can be granted to petitioner.
Even copy of the notification has not been placed on record by petitioner.
Furthermore, it is not clear whether petitioner is in possession of property in dispute or not because there is no interim order in his favour.
14. Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that no case is made out warranting interference.
15. Petition fails and is hereby dismissed.

(G.S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE S.M.
